articles.title: One Claude Code session ran 15 subagents under our 10-subagent rule. After a PreToolUse hook, 676 launches peaked at 10
articles.excerpt: For eight weeks our limit of 10 concurrent Claude Code subagents was a sentence in CLAUDE.md, and one session reached 15. A PreToolUse hook on the Agent tool now refuses the 11th by counting the subag…
articles.body: For eight weeks our limit of 10 concurrent Claude Code subagents was a sentence in CLAUDE.md, and one session reached 15. A PreToolUse hook on the Agent tool now refuses the 11th by counting the subagents still running in the session plus the launches already placed in the same response. Across 676 launches since, the peak has been exactly 10. Its first four refusals were wrong, and Claude Code's own subagent limit would not have caught our 15. A cap that was only a sentence On 2026-08-03 our agent started 56 subagents at once for a weekly review, and the Mac it runs on ran short of memory. The owner capped parallel subagents at 30 that day and lowered the cap to 10 the next day.

articles.title: I turned on Secure Boot and my Ubuntu laptop stopped booting
articles.excerpt: I have an old HP EliteBook Folio 9470m (2014, BIOS F.48) running Ubuntu. I had just upgraded to the latest version Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS resolute, and I thought I would turn on Secure Boot while I was at…
articles.body: I have an old HP EliteBook Folio 9470m (2014, BIOS F.48) running Ubuntu. I had just upgraded to the latest version Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS resolute , and I thought I would turn on Secure Boot while I was at it. I restarted and Ubuntu would not boot. I went back into the BIOS, switched Secure Boot off, and Ubuntu came up again. Then I checked the state from inside Ubuntu: mokutil --sb-state It said: Setup Mode means the firmware has no Platform Key enrolled. With no keys, Secure Boot has nothing to check anything against. i went Looking back at the BIOS, I had switched the key option from HP’s keys to “Customer Keys” and never enrolled any. My best guess is that this is what kept it in Setup Mode.

articles.body: What I Built Pocket Ledger is an offline-first receipt and invoice sorter built for freelancers, contractors, and small teams who want a faster way to organize financial paperwork without sacrificing privacy. The app lets users upload PDFs or images of receipts, extracts key details like vendor, date, amount, currency, and category using an AI model, and then automatically copies the files into organized folders. It also generates an editable CSV for bookkeeping and tax prep. This solves a real pain point: manually sorting receipts is tedious, error-prone, and time-consuming. Pocket Ledger turns that workflow into a simple “upload → review → export” process while keeping the experience local-first and flexible.

It covers the three parts of Mantle I spent the most time with: tool calling, memory, and the LLM layer . That includes running it on Groq, which Rasa doesn't list as a named provider. The VS Code extension owns the notes and exposes a tiny HTTP endpoint on localhost:37492 .

articles.title: Mitigating Silent JSON Schema Drift in Microservices: Pre-Validation Engine Patterns and the Portability Pitfall
articles.excerpt: When microservices communicate asynchronously via message brokers or REST endpoints, schema evolution is inevitable. However, without strict automated governance, small, undocumented schema alteration…
articles.body: When microservices communicate asynchronously via message brokers or REST endpoints, schema evolution is inevitable. However, without strict automated governance, small, undocumented schema alterations—known as silent schema drift —frequently cascade into catastrophic deserialization and parsing failures downstream. This article dissects the design and engineering of an automated pre-validation CLI engine built with Python, Pydantic v2, and jsonschema (Draft 2020-12). It details the architectural decisions aimed at ultra-low-latency payload verification, uncovers how strict performance mandates introduced subtle portability traps during deployment, and outlines architectural remedies for resilient pipeline design. 1.

articles.excerpt: Receiving USD payments in Pakistan as a developer: what actually works in 2026 If you're a developer in Pakistan trying to get paid by an international client or via a SaaS product, the first thing th…
articles.body: Receiving USD payments in Pakistan as a developer: what actually works in 2026 If you're a developer in Pakistan trying to get paid by an international client or via a SaaS product, the first thing that doesn't work is the thing everyone else assumes you'll use: Stripe. Stripe does not list Pakistan among its supported countries. You'll see tutorials telling you to "just sign up for Stripe," and then you'll hit a wall at onboarding that the tutorial never mentions. So let's skip Stripe and talk about what actually moves money into your account. Two separate problems, not one The mistake is thinking "I need a payment gateway." You actually need two things: A platform that will onboard you and pay you in USD. A way to bring that USD into a Pakistani bank account.

articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.body: HBO and HBO Max's " Lanterns " served up its big cliffhanger finale on Oct. 4, 2026, and we’ve been slowly digesting thoughts on what the creative direction and ultimate legacy of this debut season were. While by no means a perfect experiment in trying to shake up the aging superhero genre, there are enough worthy elements to consider this sci-fi mystery show an evolutionary step towards the next generation of comic-based storytelling. After the emerald-tinted dust has settled, there are many lingering questions about where this acclaimed series from creators Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof, and Tom King might be headed and where the twists and turns might lead for a sophomore season should it be greenlit (get it?) for a triumphant return.

articles.title: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, bringing a spectacular display of shooting stars to the autumn sky.
articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
